plan.notes: Source: official Portland State University 2025-26 Degree Map, 'Computer Science - Bachelor of Science 2025-26 Degree Map' (www.pdx.edu/registration/computer-science-bachelor-science-2025-26-degree-map), published by the PSU Registrar. The degree's true name is 'Computer Science - Bachelor of Science'; the department is the Department of Computer Science in the Maseeh College of Engineering and Computer Science. Transcribed term-by-term verbatim from the map on 2026-09-30; no courses, credits, or prereqs invented. PSU is a QUARTER school: all terms are Fall/Winter/Spring and all credits are QUARTER credits; the map states students must reach 180 total credits. Transcribed term totals (Fall/Winter/Spring: Y1 14/18/14, Y2 16/12/16, Y3 16/16/16, Y4 12/15/15) sum to exactly 180. The 'Race and Ethnic Studies Requirement' is listed as 3-4 credits; recorded at 4 so the plan totals 180, with the range documented in the slot's choice_note. Course titles for named courses verified against the official 2025-26 PSU Bulletin 'Computer Science B.S.' page (pdx.smartcatalogiq.com/2025-2026/bulletin/.../computer-science-b-s), including the approved lists for the security elective, upper-division CS electives, lab science, and math/statistics electives. Student-choice slots use choice:true with placeholder codes and descriptive titles; either/or slots (MTH 253Z or MTH 261; CS 305 or PHL 314U) are recorded as single choice slots with the options enumerated. Only one prereq is officially documented at the course level (CS 163 requires 'CS 162 with a grade of C or better', per the official bulletin course description); all other prereq fields are intentionally left empty rather than inferred. The 2025-26 bulletin also publishes a year-by-year sample curriculum whose junior/senior distributions differ slightly from this degree map (e.g. bulletin junior year totals 44 vs the map's 48); both total 180. The map carries no 2026-27 edition; the 2025-26 map is the current official term-by-term plan. The map notes: opt-in to the major during fall term of year 3 (week 8), admission to upper-division CS courses requires major admission, and junior standing (90 credits) is required for upper-division CS registration per the bulletin.
